n_clips_raw.note: Section 3.2.3 and Table 3: raw clip count

n_clips_retained.note: Section 3.2.4: clips passing the 90% landmark-quality threshold

pct_clips_padded.note: Section 3.3: share of clips shorter than the 60-frame window

mean_live_frames.note: Section 3.3: mean number of real (non-padded) frames per standardized sequence

test_per_class.note: Figure 6 caption: test samples per class

train_imbalance_ratio.note: Section 3.6 / Eq. (15): whether class weighting is justified

proposed_accuracy_mean.note: Abstract, Section 4.2, Table 7, Conclusions: headline accuracy (mean over seeds)

proposed_accuracy_std.note: Table 7: cross-seed standard deviation of the proposed model

proposed_best_accuracy.note: Section 4.2: single-run checkpointed best model, if a single figure is quoted

strongest_baseline.note: Section 4.3: the model the proposed one is compared to

margin_over_best_baseline_pp.note: Section 4.3: margin in percentage points over the strongest same-corpus baseline

proposed_best_epoch.note: Figure 4 caption: the epoch at which early stopping restored the best weights

proposed_train_val_gap_pp.note: Section 4.2: the train-validation gap behind the regularization claim

expected_calibration_error.note: Section 4.7.2: whether the confidence threshold in Algorithm 1 is trustworthy

n_baselines_significantly_beaten.note: Section 4.3: how many baselines the proposed model separates from at p<0.05

proposed_accuracy_ci.note: Abstract and Section 4.2: the 95% bootstrap interval to quote alongside the point accuracy

delta_full_face_pp.note: Section 3.2.6 (A10): measured effect of adding the full 468-landmark face stream

delta_compact_face_pp.note: Section 3.2.6 (A10): measured effect of adding the compact 40-landmark face stream

delta_hands_only_pp.note: Section 4.5 (B16): measured feature importance, NOT a linguistic claim

delta_pose_only_pp.note: Section 4.5 (B16): measured feature importance, NOT a linguistic claim

attention_entropy_ratio.note: Section 4.6: how much more selective than uniform the learned attention is

attention_top10_mass.note: Section 4.6: share of attention mass on the ten most salient frames

signer_dependent_accuracy.note: Abstract and Section 4.2: the headline figure, scoped to unseen repetitions by known signers

signer_independent_accuracy.note: Section 4.1 and 4.7.1 (B15): leave-one-signer-out accuracy, to be reported alongside the headline figure

signer_generalization_gap_pp.note: Section 4.7.1 (B15): how much of the headline figure depends on having seen the signer during training

proposed_parameters.note: Abstract, Table 5, Table 10, Table 11, Section 4.7.2: the true parameter count

proposed_macs_per_clip_M.note: Section 4.7.2: computational cost per clip, if a complexity figure is quoted

extraction_ms_per_frame.note: Section 4.7.2 (B14): the cost that determines whether the pipeline is interactive

inference_ms_cpu.note: Section 4.7.2 (B14): classifier latency per clip on CPU

end_to_end_ms_cpu.note: Section 4.7.2 (B14): end-to-end delay for one clip on CPU

real_time_verdict.note: Section 4.7.1 (B14): whether the term "real-time" is defensible at all

tts_parameters.note: Section 3.7: size of the pretrained synthesizer, for contrast with the recognition model. Makes the point that the large component is the one this study did not train.

tts_mean_latency_ms.note: Section 4.7.2: synthesis latency, if end-to-end interaction cost is quoted

release_dataset_mb.note: Data Availability Statement: size of the releasable landmark corpus
